skills.name: godot_character_body_controller_3d
skills.skill: Implement robust kinematic character controllers using CharacterBody3D and Godot 4.7 motion APIs
procedure: Create a CharacterBody3D node with a CollisionShape3D (CapsuleShape3D) and visual hierarchy.
In _physics_process(delta), compute gravitational acceleration: velocity.y -= ProjectSettings.get_setting('physics/3d/default_gravity') * delta when not is_on_floor().
Derive horizontal direction from player input relative to the active Camera3D basis: direction = (camera_basis * Vector3(input_x, 0, input_z)).normalized().
Apply smooth acceleration and deceleration using velocity.move_toward() or lerp on horizontal velocity components (x and z).
Call move_and_slide() without parameters (Godot 4 uses internal velocity state).
Inspect collision data via get_slide_collision_count() and get_slide_collision() for impact responses, platform interaction, and slope handling.
verification: Run headless tests asserting is_on_floor() returns true on static bodies.
Verify character slides smoothly up floor_max_angle slopes without jitter.
Check terminal velocities under continuous falling to ensure no NaN/INF propagation in velocity vector.
pitfalls: Passing velocity to move_and_slide(); in Godot 4, move_and_slide takes no arguments and mutates the internal velocity property directly.
Failing to flatten camera transform basis vectors before calculating ground velocity, causing unintended vertical thrust when looking up or down.
Modifying global_transform.origin directly instead of setting velocity, breaking continuous collision detection.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Create a complete GDScript for a 3D first-person CharacterBody3D that supports 8-direction WASD movement, jumping with variable jump height, slope walking up to 45 degrees, and camera-relative motion, compatible with Godot 4.7.2.

skills.name: godot_procedural_grid_pathfinding_2d
skills.skill: Build dynamic 2D grid-based navigation using AStarGrid2D with obstacle avoidance and weight masks
procedure: Instantiate an AStarGrid2D instance via GDScript.
Define grid boundaries and cell dimensions using region (Rect2i) and cell_size (Vector2).
Set diagonal_mode (e.g., DIAGONAL_MODE_AT_LEAST_ONE_WALKABLE or DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER) and heuristic calculation.
Call update() to initialize internal navigation memory structures.
Mark static obstacles and TileMap collisions using set_point_solid(coords, true) or clear_point_weight_scale().
Query paths on demand with get_point_path(from_coord, to_coord) or get_id_path(from_coord, to_coord).
Dynamically toggle point solid state in response to runtime gameplay events (e.g., doors opening, destructible objects).
verification: Assert path result is non-empty for reachable adjacent coordinates.
Assert path avoids coordinates set as solid via set_point_solid().
Profile path query times over a 256x256 grid ensuring latency remains below 1ms per query.
pitfalls: Forgetting to call astar_grid.update() after configuring region or cell_size, resulting in empty path arrays.
Passing world coordinates directly instead of converted grid coordinates (Vector2i) to get_point_path().
Re-initializing the entire grid per frame instead of mutating solid flags incrementally.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Implement a GDScript class GridNavigator2D wrapping AStarGrid2D for a 100x100 tile world. Expose methods to toggle obstacles, update cell weights for terrain penalties, and retrieve world-space Vector2 paths smoothed for CharacterBody2D navigation.

skills.name: godot_animation_tree_statemachine_blend
skills.skill: Configure and control layered 3D character animations via AnimationTree and AnimationNodeStateMachine
procedure: Attach an AnimationPlayer to the skeleton scene containing all required asset animations.
Add an AnimationTree node, set anim_player path to the AnimationPlayer, and assign tree_root to an AnimationNodeStateMachine or AnimationNodeBlendTree.
Construct state nodes (e.g., Idle, Run, Jump, Fall) and configure AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition with appropriate switch mode and xfade_time.
For locomotion, nest an AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D inside locomotion states to blend horizontal/vertical movement blends.
In the character script, retrieve the playback controller: state_machine = animation_tree.get('parameters/playback').
Update state machine parameters dynamically: call state_machine.travel('Run') and animation_tree.set('parameters/Run/blend_position', input_vector).
Activate the AnimationTree node (active = true).
verification: Verify state transitions complete smoothly without visual frame pops using blend cross-fade checks.
Check animation_tree.get('parameters/playback').get_current_node() matches expected state during simulated physics steps.
pitfalls: Querying parameter paths with typos; paths are string-based and fail silently or return null if unverified.
Setting active = true on AnimationTree before the AnimationPlayer has valid animation libraries registered.
Calling state_machine.travel() every frame with the same state string, which can inadvertently reset non-looping transitions if auto-restart conditions match.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Write a GDScript helper that initializes an AnimationTree programmatically with an AnimationNodeStateMachine containing 'Idle' and 'Move' states, an active transition with 0.2s crossfade, and provides a clean API to blend locomotion velocity.

skills.name: godot_polyphonic_audio_synthesis
skills.skill: Implement low-latency, dynamic polyphonic SFX playback using AudioStreamPolyphonic and AudioServer
procedure: Instantiate an AudioStreamPolyphonic resource and configure polyphony capacity (number of concurrent voices).
Assign the polyphonic resource to an AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D, or AudioStreamPlayer3D.
Ensure the AudioStreamPlayer is started via play() to obtain an active playback instance.
Acquire the stream playback interface: playback = player.get_stream_playback() as AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.
Trigger audio samples using playback.play_stream(stream, from_offset, volume_db, pitch_scale).
Store stream playback IDs to dynamically adjust pitch, volume, or stop active voices via playback.set_stream_pitch_scale(id, pitch) and playback.stop_stream(id).
verification: Assert playback is not null and is of type AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.
Trigger rapid concurrent sound bursts and verify voice count does not exceed allocated polyphony or cause audio underruns.
Confirm voice pitch modulation reflects immediately without restarting the stream.
pitfalls: Calling player.get_stream_playback() before player.play() is invoked, which returns null.
Exceeding maximum configured voices in AudioStreamPolyphonic, resulting in dropped sound triggers.
Storing voice IDs across scene changes or after streams naturally finish playing.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Develop an AudioManager autoload script in GDScript utilizing AudioStreamPolyphonic on Godot 4.7.2 that pools SFX streams, prevents sound spamming with a cooldown table, and modulates pitch randomly between 0.95 and 1.05.

skills.name: godot_surface_tool_procedural_mesh
skills.skill: Generate optimized procedural 3D runtime geometry using SurfaceTool and ArrayMesh
procedure: Instantiate a SurfaceTool object via SurfaceTool.new().
Begin primitive construction with st.begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES).
For each vertex, define attributes prior to the vertex position: st.set_normal(), st.set_uv(), st.set_color(), followed by st.add_vertex(position).
Generate triangle indices using st.add_index() to allow vertex reuse across shared edges.
Call st.generate_normals() and st.generate_tangents() if vertex attributes were not manually calculated.
Commit the geometry into an ArrayMesh via st.commit().
Assign the generated ArrayMesh to a MeshInstance3D and apply a BaseMaterial3D.
verification: Inspect committed mesh surface count with array_mesh.get_surface_count() == 1.
Check triangle vertex count and index count match the planned geometric topology.
Validate presence of normals and tangents by inspecting Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL and Mesh.ARRAY_TANGENT arrays.
pitfalls: Calling st.set_uv() or st.set_normal() after st.add_vertex(); attribute setters must precede the vertex they apply to.
Failing to specify indices when building complex watertight geometry, causing massive vertex redundancy and broken smooth shading.
Invoking generate_tangents() without valid UV coordinates on the surface, which causes runtime errors.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Write a GDScript tool script that procedurally generates a subdivided UV sphere mesh using SurfaceTool, computes smooth normals and UV coordinates, commits to an ArrayMesh, and generates an optimized collision shape via create_trimesh_shape().

skills.name: godot_custom_compositor_post_process
skills.skill: Create custom screen-space post-processing pipelines using Godot 4.7 CompositorEffect and RenderingDevice
procedure: Create a custom resource script extending CompositorEffect.
Set access_resolved_color and access_resolved_depth flags depending on render pass requirements.
Override _render_callback(effect_callback_type, render_data) to hook into the Godot render graph.
Retrieve the RenderingDevice: rd = RenderingServer.get_rendering_device().
Extract the render scene buffers via render_data.get_render_scene_buffers().
Bind compute pipelines, uniform sets, and screen textures, then dispatch compute shaders across the screen dimensions.
Attach the custom CompositorEffect resource to a Compositor assigned to Camera3D or WorldEnvironment.
verification: Ensure _render_callback only executes when render_data is valid.
Verify compute shader dispatches match target viewport dimensions: ceil(size.x / workgroup_size_x).
Confirm absence of GPU sync stalls and validation layer errors in debug output.
pitfalls: Retaining RenderingDevice RID handles across frame reconstitutions without tracking lifecycle.
Dispatching compute shaders on incompatible callback stages (e.g., using stage EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PRE_OPAQUE for post-tonemap effects).
Forgetting synchronization barriers when reading and writing to the same scene buffer.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Create a custom CompositorEffect in GDScript for Godot 4.7.2 that accesses the resolved color buffer and executes a simple compute shader to invert screen colors at the post-transparent stage.

skills.name: godot_procedural_ik_bone_modifiers
skills.skill: Configure procedural inverse kinematics and bone constraints using SkeletonModifier3D and IKModifier3D nodes
procedure: Identify the Skeleton3D node within the imported character hierarchy.
Add skeletal modifier nodes as direct children of Skeleton3D (e.g., CCDIK3D, ChainIK3D, AimModifier3D, BoneTwistDisperser3D).
Set modifier target nodes or transform nodes (e.g., marker or target Node3D representing hand reach or look-at targets).
Specify bone chains by configuring the root bone name and tip bone name using valid skeleton bone names.
Adjust solver parameters such as iterations, tolerance, and angle limits to ensure natural deformation.
Enable the modifier via active = true and tune influence dynamically during gameplay interactions.
verification: Verify that tip bone transform tracks target marker position during runtime physics steps.
Check that bone twists along joint chains do not produce flipped or collapsing meshes when limits are reached.
Ensure modifier execution order under Skeleton3D reflects intended dependencies (e.g., twisting after IK solving).
pitfalls: Adding SkeletonModifier3D nodes outside of the Skeleton3D subtree; modifiers must be children of the Skeleton3D.
Specifying misspelled bone names; use skeleton.find_bone(name) to validate bone indices before assignment.
Running conflicting IK modifiers simultaneously on overlapping bone segments without properly weighted influence values.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Write a GDScript setup that configures an AimModifier3D and a ChainIK3D on a humanoid Skeleton3D to make the head track the player's crosshair and the arm reach towards an interactable 3D handle.
